title: TLS: Add a stream id
description:
Track stream ID numbers for TLS. Create one for every session
(including sessions from external information, but *not* TLS
handshake-only sessions created for QUIC that will never have
real appdata.) Add it to the tree as a generated item.

This makes "Follow Stream" for TLS work better; the Follow Dialog
won't select TCP streams that have no TLS, and it should allow
finding the TLS stream to follow on packets where the port type at
the end of the frame is not TCP (either because the TLS is over
SCTP, or the port type changes in the application data due to
tunnelling, or something else.)

notes.body: Can we cache the result of find_dissector("tls") so it doesn't have to keep looking up the same answer for every packet?

Yes we can, and I thought about that. Though do note that it's not "every packet," it's only when once per TLS stream on the first pass when it creates a new session because the existing conversation lookup failed.
I would definitely have cached it if it was doing the look up every packet.
(There is a minor "what if someone calls `deregister_dissector("tls")` in other code not at startup for some crazy reason" edge case, but hopefully that wouldn't happen.)
There was a point in time where I moved many find_dissector() calls to dissector handoff functions.  I thought that was a better home for it (and removes the need for an if statement)
Right. The thing here is that both the TLS and the DTLS dissector use this function so it makes it a bit complicated.

I don't love any of the solutions that involve the TLS dissector calling something in its handoff and the DTLS dissector in its. And storing it in another data structure isn't all that much better than this rare lookup.
I moved it to a handoff function created for tls-utils.
